body:
Observed on a live `pdca flow` Check review (codex `exec` reviewer leaf): the reviewer wrote check-review.md, then composed one compound self-validation script — rg row-counts asserting all eleven 5/5/1 rows and their verdicts, a line-count sanity check — ending with `rm -rf` of a scratch dir it had created for itself under `/var/tmp/pdca/pdca-reviewer-<id>-*` (case-guarded to its own path). codex's command policy refused the WHOLE script before executing any of it:

```
ERROR codex_core::tools::router: error=exec_command failed for '/bin/bash -lc ...'
rejected: rm -f style commands are not permitted. Use a safer approach
```

Per-run this is benign — rejected at spawn, nothing half-executed, the leaf continued and the heartbeat resumed. But it is systematic, not a one-off:

- `agents/reviewer.md` says nothing about sandbox ownership, so a conscientious model invents scratch OUTSIDE its cwd and then feels obliged to delete it;
- codex exec's policy bans rm-style commands unconditionally in this mode, so **every** codex reviewer cycle that self-cleans pays a wasted model round-trip (and may loop hunting a "safer approach");
- the scratch dir leaks into /var/tmp when the model gives up.

The harness already owns the lifecycle the model is trying to manage: the reviewer's cwd is a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="pdca-review-")` (leaves.py), auto-deleted when the leaf exits — anything inside it needs zero cleanup.

Proposed fix: add a scratch-discipline line to the canonical `template/agents/reviewer.md` body — work only inside your cwd; never create files outside it; never run rm-style cleanup — your cwd is a disposable sandbox the harness deletes for you. The body is inlined for codex and wrapped for claude, so every vendor inherits it. Worth considering the same line for the other headless-leaf bodies (the builder edits the harness-managed $PDCA_WORKTREE; the advisory reviewers share the reviewer sandbox shape).

comments.body:
Flagging an interaction before this gets implemented: #422 argues the remedy here — *"your cwd is a disposable sandbox the harness deletes for you"* — is right about ownership but, taken alone, makes cold rebuilds permanent.

The cwd is `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="pdca-review-")` (`leaves.py:1795`), deleted per leaf. `agents/reviewer.md` simultaneously requires the reviewer to re-run the evidence itself (`reviewer.md.jinja:24-25`). If the only sanctioned location is deleted every run, no build cache can ever survive, so every review recompiles the target from cold.

Measured cost of that on one live Check (wyrd-pdca, 2026-08-02, two reviewers in parallel for ~13 min): ~69 GB written, 19 GB of it a single cold `cargo-target-ci`. It flooded the cgroup's page cache and systemd-oomd killed the whole `pdca flow` run — see #420 and getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#199.

So the scratch the model is inventing under `/var/tmp/pdca/pdca-reviewer-<id>-*` isn't only a leak and a wasted round-trip; it's also the model reaching for the persistence the sandbox doesn't give it. #422 proposes splitting the two lifetimes — keep this issue's disposable per-run cwd exactly as described, and add a lane-stable, harness-owned, swept build-cache root the prompt line can point *at* rather than only away from.

Worth landing the two together, so the prompt gains a sanctioned destination in the same change that forbids the improvised one.

title: agents/reviewer.md: forbid self-made scratch + rm-style cleanup — codex exec rejects it every cycle
